paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The people of Jerusalem did a LOT of work. They patched the walls, collected water from the lower pool, and tore down houses to strengthen the wall (Isaiah 22:9-10). But the prophet says they "did not look to the One who made it, or consider Him who planned it long ago" (Isaiah 22:11). All that effort, and God was the one thing missing from the plan.

Then comes the part that hurts. The Lord GOD of Hosts called for weeping and wailing, and the people answered with eating and drinking: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!" (Isaiah 22:12-13). I think the heaviest thing here is that they saw death coming and still turned away from the mourning God called for. The prophet, though, weeps bitterly over the destruction of his people (Isaiah 22:4).

So what do we do with this, baker? Be careful about trusting your own busy hands more than the God who made everything. Plan, work, fix what's broken, but look to Him first, and when He calls you to turn to Him, answer instead of putting it off. That's why my ovens stay ready: when He calls, I want to be found looking to Him.
